package_info.package_manager: N/A (custom malware/backdoor, not a public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: WINELOADER is a custom backdoor deployed via a malicious PDF in a targeted cyber espionage campaign (SPIKEDWINE) against European diplomats. It is designed to provide remote access and control to attackers, enabling data theft and persistent compromise.

execution_context.trigger: user opens malicious PDF (initial infection vector)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Embedded PDF exploit code that, when opened, executes a payload to drop and run the WINELOADER backdoor.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon opening the PDF, the embedded exploit executes code that writes the WINELOADER backdoor to disk and launches it, establishing initial persistence and command-and-control communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: PDFs should not execute arbitrary code or drop executables. The use of a document as a malware delivery vector is a hallmark of targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDFs are static documents; this one contains active exploit code and a payload.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate scenario for a PDF to drop and execute a backdoor.

execution_context.file_location: dropped WINELOADER binary (location varies, e.g., %TEMP% or user profile directory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: WINELOADER backdoor code that establishes persistence, connects to C2, and awaits commands.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After execution, the WINELOADER backdoor establishes persistence on the victim system, connects to a remote command-and-control server, and awaits further instructions, enabling remote access and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary establishes unauthorized remote access and persistence, typical of espionage malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently connect to external C2 servers or await attacker commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools (RATs) may have similar functionality, but are not delivered via phishing PDFs to diplomats.
key_indicators: Persistence mechanisms (e.g., registry run keys, scheduled tasks)

attack_chain.action: Victim receives spear-phishing email with malicious PDF attachment disguised as an invitation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens the PDF, triggering the exploit.

attack_chain.action: Malicious PDF executes embedded exploit code to drop and run the WINELOADER backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: WINELOADER backdoor is installed and executed.

attack_chain.action: WINELOADER establishes persistence and connects to the attacker's command-and-control infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access and can exfiltrate data or issue further commands.

behavioral_signatures: PDF documents that drop and execute binaries upon opening
Unexpected process creation from PDF reader applications
Outbound connections to suspicious C2 infrastructure after opening a document
Persistence mechanisms created shortly after document open events
file_indicators: PDF attachments with embedded exploit code
Unknown executables dropped in user profile or temp directories after PDF open
Registry or scheduled task entries referencing new binaries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to previously unseen domains or IPs after document open
C2 traffic patterns (e.g., beaconing, encrypted payloads) from endpoints that opened suspicious PDFs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PDF files that, when opened, result in the creation and execution of new binaries. Correlate process creation events from PDF readers with subsequent network connections to suspicious domains or IPs. Look for persistence mechanisms established shortly after document open events, and scan for unknown binaries in user directories. Use endpoint protection and sandboxing to detect exploit behavior in document files.
